html:
The Clatskanie, or Tlatskanai, were a small Athabaskan people of the Clatskanie and upper Nehalem rivers in northwestern Oregon, south of the lower Columbia. Their language was the same as that of the Kwalhioqua across the river in Washington, and the two are thought to have once been one people.

They lived as hunters in the hills behind the Chinook villages on the Columbia. Epidemics in the 1830s nearly destroyed them, and the few survivors joined neighbouring peoples. The town and river of Clatskanie in Columbia County, Oregon, keep their name.
